label: Scarborough Shoal — Possible Chinese Structure Visible May 27-30, Disappeared by June 1 (Philippines Probe Day 3, Jun 5)
sub: Reuters satellite analysis (June 4) confirmed a small reflective object — consistent with a 'floating raft or buoy' — appeared at Scarborough Shoal's southern lagoon entrance in Vantor/SeaLight imagery May 27-30 but was absent from June 1 imagery, suggesting possible removal ahead of scrutiny. Philippines launched formal probe June 3 (Teodoro, Brawner). China silent for 3+ days. NTF-WPS conducting overflights. The object follows China's April 2026 352-meter floating barrier at the same location — part of a layered incremental control strategy. Sources: Reuters via Star-Advertiser, BusinessWorld, Interaksyon/Philstar, Newsweek, Naval News (June 2026).

label: China CCG Patrol — East of Taiwan (Jun 1, 2026): Response to Japan-Philippines Maritime Boundary Talks
sub: China Coast Guard deployed patrols in waters east of Taiwan on June 1, 2026, declaring it 'a necessary action' in response to Japan and the Philippines formally launching maritime boundary delimitation talks following the Takaichi-Marcos summit in Tokyo on May 29. China's FM called the Japan-Philippines talks 'completely illegal, null and void.' Taiwan's foreign ministry countered that China has 'no right to interfere.' The patrols extend China's gray zone coercion from the South China Sea into the western Pacific — a new front simultaneous with the Scarborough Shoal, Second Thomas Shoal, and Pag-asa Island standoffs. Sources: Jakarta Post, Japan Times, Nippon.com (June 1, 2026).

label: Pratas / Dongsha Islands — Taiwan-China CCG 33-Hour Standoff (May 24-25, 2026)
sub: Taiwan Coast Guard patrol vessel Taichung (1,000 tons) and China's CCG-3501 (5,500 tons) engaged in a 33-hour standoff near Taiwan-administered Pratas/Dongsha Islands on May 24-25, 2026. The confrontation followed China's post-Trump-Xi summit deployment of 100+ vessels across the first island chain. CCG-3501 departed at 5 PM May 25 after radio challenges; no kinetic incident. Security analysts flagged the vulnerability of Pratas (400+ km from Taiwan main island) and the multi-theater CCG escalation strategy paralleling China's simultaneous WPS pressure against the Philippines.

label: CCG 4305 — Unauthorized EEZ Patrol Off Zambales (May 19-21, 2026)
sub: China Coast Guard vessel CCG 4305 detected ~48 nautical miles west of Pandaquit, Zambales by Canada's Dark Vessel Detection (DVS) Program on May 19, 2026. PCG aircraft Piper Navajo 302 confirmed position and issued radio challenges; BRP Cape San Agustin deployed for surface challenge. CCG 4305 remained in Philippine EEZ for three days (May 19-21) before withdrawing after sustained PCG radio challenges. First documented CCG unauthorized patrol along the Luzon western coast; extends China's multi-front WPS pressure beyond traditional Spratly/Scarborough dispute zones to the Luzon littoral.

label: PLA Task Group 107 Exercise Area — East of Luzon
sub: PLA Southern Theater Command Naval Task Group 107 conducted live-fire drills, sea-air coordination, rapid maneuvers, and maritime replenishments in waters east of Luzon Island, Philippines, April 24–25, 2026. Described by PLA as 'a necessary action in response to the current regional situation' (Balikatan 2026). This eastern Luzon deployment directly flanks the Philippine Sea approach — complementing China's simultaneous SCS counter-posture: Liaoning carrier group, Type 076 Sichuan, and the 133rd Task Group Pacific circuit.

label: Antelope Reef (Paracel Islands) — 2026 Construction
sub: CSIS AMTI (May 2026) confirmed China's first major artificial island construction since 2017 at Antelope Reef (Lingyang Jiao), Paracel Islands. Reclaimed area ~1,490 acres — now potentially the largest island in the South China Sea, rivaling or surpassing Mischief Reef (1,504 acres). Northwestern edge has straight outer profile consistent with a future 9,000-ft airstrip (heavier than the 3,000m runways at Fiery Cross/Subi/Mischief). 50+ grey-roofed structures, helipad, jetties, and potential SAM/ASCM battery foundations documented. Construction accelerated April 2026 as US SCS recon flights dropped ~30% amid Middle East redeployments (Asia Times, April 4). Vietnam filed diplomatic protest March 23. China claims Paracels as sovereign territory 'not in dispute.' UPDATE (Aug 19, 2026): Reuters satellite imagery confirmed China completed the first construction stage — a reclaimed island ~6km long with a 3km+ straight coastline, a 680m wharf, deep-water harbor, and helipad in the southeast corner; dredgers and barges have departed after 6+ months of work. Analysts (PLATracker's Ben Lewis) say the site is 'ideally placed' for a Taiwan conflict scenario and could host H-6 strategic bombers, forming part of China's largest South China Sea military base. China's defense ministry has not acknowledged the base; state media describe the site's purpose as weather forecasting and scientific research.

label: Fiery Cross Reef (Yongshu Jiao)
sub: China's primary Spratly command hub with 3,125m runway, hardened aircraft shelters for 24+ fighters, HQ-9B SAMs, and YJ-12B anti-ship missiles. Reclamation of ~677 acres completed 2015.

label: Fiery Cross — HQ-9B SAM Site
sub: HQ-9B long-range surface-to-air missile batteries deployed May 2018. Coverage radius ~160 nm; threatens all aircraft over the central South China Sea. Violates Xi Jinping's 2015 pledge to Obama not to militarize the features.

label: Mischief Reef (Meiji Jiao)
sub: Largest of China's three major Spratly outposts (~1,379 acres reclaimed). Constructed within the Philippines' EEZ; seizure from Philippines in 1995 was a turning point in SCS militarization. HQ-9B and YJ-12B weapons deployed since 2018.

label: Mischief Reef — Artillery Emplacements
sub: CSIS AMTI (2023) documented three sets of three hardened emplacements along the western and northern edges, suitable for mobile artillery or rocket launchers. Equipment periodically deployed under tarps. Part of ongoing Spratly Island fortification program.

label: Subi Reef (Zhubi Jiao)
sub: 976 acres reclaimed; located 16 nm southwest of Philippine-held Thitu Island. China's northernmost major Spratly outpost. HQ-9B SAMs and YJ-12B ASCMs deployed 2018. Two new radomes added 2023–2024 for ISR coverage of the SCS.

label: Subi Reef — Airstrip & Hangar Complex
sub: 3,000m runway with aircraft hangars. ISR and EW upgrades 2023–2024 include fixed monopole antenna arrays targeting multiple electromagnetic spectrum bands. AMTI: represents China's 'integrated strategy to establish unmatched ISR dominance.'

label: Johnson South Reef (Chigua Jiao)
sub: ~10 acres reclaimed. Site of March 14, 1988 'Johnson South Reef Skirmish' in which China killed approximately 70 Vietnamese sailors and seized the reef—China's first armed seizure of a Spratly feature. Now a small military outpost with anti-aircraft weapons.

label: Gaven Reef North (Nanxun Jiao)
sub: 86 acres reclaimed. Armed with anti-aircraft guns, naval guns, and search radars. Lighthouse built. China has occupied Gaven Reef since 1988; current outpost hosts barracks, radar systems, and communications equipment.

label: Hughes Reef (Dongmen Jiao)
sub: 7.6 acres reclaimed; Chinese outpost since 1988. Armed with anti-aircraft weapons. One of six Spratly features occupied by China before the major 2013–2016 reclamation drive. Receives Chinese maritime militia vessels operating in the Spratly waters.

label: Woody Island (Yongxing Dao) — China Paracel HQ
sub: China's largest Paracel outpost and seat of Sansha City administration (established 2012). 213 ha; 1,000+ military/civilian residents; 2,700m runway. HQ-9 SAMs deployed since February 2016, triggering US protests. China administers all Paracel Islands from this island.

label: Woody Island — Military Airfield
sub: 2,700m runway capable of hosting J-11 fighters, H-6 bombers, and KJ-500 AEW aircraft. China has deployed fighter jets to Woody Island for exercises, directly threatening Vietnam's SCS claims. Also hosts long-range radar systems monitoring Paracel and northern Spratly waters.

label: Yulin Naval Base — Hainan Island
sub: China's primary South Sea Fleet submarine base, with underground submarine pens carved into the mountain. Houses Type 094 Jin-class SSBNs and Type 093 Shang-class SSNs. Key forward deployment point for PLAN submarines operating in the South China Sea.

label: Zhanjiang — PLA South Sea Fleet HQ
sub: Headquarters of the PLA Navy's Southern Theater Command Navy (South Sea Fleet). Major surface combatant homeport. Zhanjiang Naval Academy also located here. Primary command and logistics center for China's South China Sea operations.

label: Pattle Island — China Paracel Outpost
sub: Second-largest island in China's Paracel Island chain. Hosts a weather station, military garrison, and communications equipment. China has administered the Paracel Islands since seizing them from South Vietnam in a 1974 battle that killed dozens of Vietnamese sailors.

label: Duncan Island — China Paracel Outpost
sub: Small island in the southwestern Paracel group; occupied by China since 1974. Hosts a military garrison and monitoring equipment. Vietnam continues to claim the entire Paracel Islands group as 'Hoang Sa archipelago.'

label: Triton Island — Southern Paracel Outpost
sub: Southernmost major island of the Paracel group. China-occupied since 1974. Site of controversial April 2020 Vietnamese fishing boat sinking by CCG vessel Haijing 4301, which rammed and sank QNg-90617 TS in waters near this island.

label: China Coast Guard — South Sea Base
sub: CCG southern operations center in the Guangdong/Hainan region. Coordinates CCG patrols, intercept operations, and law enforcement activities throughout the South China Sea. China's CCG has 500+ vessels fleet-wide, the world's largest coast guard.

label: Spratly Islands — EW/ISR Network Hub
sub: Coordinated electronic warfare and intelligence surveillance network across all three major Chinese Spratly outposts. New EW systems identified 2023–2024 at Fiery Cross, Subi, and Mischief Reefs target different electromagnetic bands. AMTI calls it an 'integrated strategy for unmatched ISR dominance.'

label: Hainan Island — PLA Military Complex
sub: China's key forward base for South China Sea operations. Hosts Yulin Naval Base (nuclear submarines), Sanya air base (H-6 bombers, surveillance aircraft), and multiple radar/signals intelligence installations. China announced Hainan's first jet carrier CNS Fujian completed sea trials from Hainan shipyards.

label: Sansha City Administrative Center
sub: China established Sansha City on Woody Island in July 2012 to administer all South China Sea island groups. In April 2020, China further subdivided it into Xisha District (Paracels) and Nansha District (Spratlys)—a formal administrative assertion of sovereignty over disputed waters. Vietnam and Philippines both protested.

label: BRP Sierra Madre — Second Thomas Shoal
sub: WWII-era US Navy tank landing ship deliberately grounded at Second Thomas Shoal (Ayungin Shoal) in 1999. Garrisoned by ~12 Philippine Marines. Hull in critical condition with large holes and severe corrosion. China has blocked/harassed at least 10 resupply missions since 2021 using water cannons, ramming, and in June 2024, bladed weapons.

label: Pag-asa Island (Thitu) — Philippines
sub: Philippines' largest occupied Spratly feature (37.2 ha). Only Spratly island with a civilian population; hosts Rancudo Airfield and Naval Station Emilio Liwanag. On April 9, 2026, the Philippines activated the new Coast Guard District Kalayaan Island Group here — the first dedicated PCG district command in the Spratly Islands. China fired flares at Philippine patrol aircraft overhead on the same day. Surrounded by Chinese maritime militia since 2017. Located 16 nm from China's Subi Reef outpost. Satellite imagery (RFA/EurasiaReview, May 8-11, 2026) confirmed a ~200m runway extension project underway at Rancudo Airfield over previously submerged land, funded at ₱1.65B ($29M) — potentially enabling F-16V operations from the Spratlys for the first time when complete.

label: Scarborough Shoal (Panatag / Huangyan)
sub: De facto Chinese control since 2012 standoff. 2016 PCA ruling found it a 'rock' not entitled to EEZ; China rejects ruling. CCG continuously present at lagoon entrance; Filipino fishermen routinely harassed with water cannons. Analysts warn Chinese permanent construction here would complete a strategic triangle with Paracels and Spratlys. UPDATE (Aug 21, 2026): PLA Southern Theater Command said it tracked, monitored and issued verbal warnings to three small Philippine government aircraft (an Islander, a Cessna C-208, and a PA-31T) that it said 'illegally intruded' into airspace over the shoal without Chinese approval, calling the flights a 'serious violation' of sovereignty. The Philippine embassy in Beijing did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

label: Whitsun Reef (Julian Felipe Reef) — 2021 Swarming
sub: ~220 Chinese blue-hulled vessels occupied this boomerang-shaped reef (12 km long) beginning December 2020, discovered by Philippines March 7, 2021. Vessels made no fishing activity, maintained military-style formations. Philippines filed 84 protests; China claimed 'fishing boats sheltering from weather.' Within Philippines' EEZ.

label: Sabina Shoal (Escoda Shoal) — 2024 Standoff
sub: Philippines deployed BRP Teresa Magbanua April 2024 after suspected Chinese reclamation activity. By August 2024, China deployed 40 ships including 3 PLAN warships; BRP Teresa Magbanua was rammed August 31, sustaining structural hull damage. Philippines withdrew September 15, 2024. Described as 'most violent, dangerous point' in Philippines-China ties.

label: Reed Bank (Recto Bank) — Active SCS Flashpoint (Day 11 Standoff)
sub: Underwater atoll hosting the most promising gas deposits in the Philippines' EEZ (~85 nm from Palawan; Service Contract 72, est. 5.4B bbl oil equivalent). A 2019 Chinese vessel rammed and sank Philippine fishing boat FB Gem-Ver here, abandoning 22 fishermen. China has blocked Philippine gas exploration here since 2019. On May 7, 2026, China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 began unauthorized marine scientific research near Iroquois Reef (southern Reed Bank) — opening a third concurrent active SCS flashpoint alongside Second Thomas Shoal and Scarborough Shoal. The Philippines filed an UNCLOS Article 246 note verbale on May 11; Beijing has not responded. As of May 17 (Day 11), the standoff continues: longest documented Chinese research vessel incursion into the Philippine EEZ without kinetic response. (Manila Times, SCMP, Rappler, May 2026)

label: Patag Island (Flat Island) — Philippines
sub: 0.57 ha Philippines-held cay in the Spratlys. Small garrison maintained. Located near Chinese-controlled Hughes and McKennan Reefs. Part of the contested Philippines-administered Kalayaan Island Group.

label: Lawak Island (Nanshan Island) — Philippines
sub: Philippines-held island (0.38 ha) in the Spratlys, classified as part of Kalayaan municipality in Palawan. Hosts a small military garrison. China, Taiwan, and Vietnam also claim the island. Located within Chinese missile coverage range from all three major Spratly outposts. Satellite imagery (RFA, May 8, 2026) confirmed a sheltered harbor construction project underway at Lawak, funded at ₱1B ($18M), to replace a shallow vessel entry channel — improving logistics and sustainment for Philippine Spratly patrol operations.

label: Loaita Island (Kota Island) — Philippines
sub: Philippines-administered island in the Spratlys. 0.39 ha; one of the smaller Philippine-held features. Military garrison maintained. Located adjacent to Philippines-claimed areas of the Kalayaan Island Group.

label: Likas Island (West York Island) — Philippines
sub: Philippines-held island (18.6 ha) in the northeastern Spratlys. Hosts a small airstrip and military garrison. Part of the Philippines' administrative territory under Kalayaan municipality. One of the more substantial Philippine-held Spratly features.

label: Scarborough Shoal — CCG Blockade Point
sub: China Coast Guard maintains continuous presence at the southeastern entrance to Scarborough Shoal's lagoon, blocking Filipino fishermen. Water cannon incidents: December 2023 (damaged 3 vessels), April 30, 2024 (during Balikatan exercises), October 8, 2024 (sailor injured, USNI video published). PLAN warships shadowed Philippine vessels in December 2024 for first time.

label: Puerto Princesa — Resupply Staging Base
sub: Capital of Palawan province and primary staging area for Philippine resupply missions to BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal. Philippine Navy and Coast Guard vessels depart from here. Distance to Second Thomas Shoal: approximately 105 nautical miles. China's blocking operations target convoys originating from this area.

label: El Nido, Palawan — Northern Patrol Base
sub: Northern Palawan town used as an additional staging area for Philippine Coast Guard and Navy patrols to the Kalayaan Island Group and Thitu Island. Also coordinates resupply missions to Pag-asa Island. Experienced growth in military presence under Marcos administration.

label: Subic Bay — Philippine Naval Base
sub: Former major US naval base (closed 1992); now Subic Bay Freeport Zone with Philippine Navy re-expanding presence. Key logistics hub for Philippine naval operations. Under Marcos administration, discussions resumed about potential return of limited US naval presence. 95 km northwest of Manila.

label: Manila — Philippine National Capital
sub: Political and military command center of the Philippines. Hosts AFP General Headquarters at Camp Aguinaldo, Philippine Coast Guard HQ, and Philippine DFA where diplomatic protests against China are filed and processed. Site of summoning Chinese Ambassador after each major SCS incident.

label: Batanes Islands — Northernmost Philippines
sub: Philippines' northernmost island group, located in the Luzon Strait separating Luzon from Taiwan (~150 km). Site of US NMESIS anti-ship missile deployment during Balikatan 2025. Strategic chokepoint for any Chinese naval transit between the Pacific and South China Sea. Coveted by US military planners for its proximity to Taiwan.

label: Second Thomas Shoal — Approach Corridor
sub: The contested maritime approach used by Philippine resupply missions to reach BRP Sierra Madre. China's CCG typically deploys 14+ vessels (as of 2023) to intercept resupply convoys along this corridor. At least 7 uses of force by China documented in the 9 months from October 2023 to June 2024 in this area.

label: Benito Ebuen Air Base — Cebu
sub: One of the original five EDCA (Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement) sites. Located on Mactan Island near Cebu City. Provides US forces with access to an air base strategically positioned between the Sulu Sea and South China Sea. Hosts Philippine Air Force fighter and transport units.

label: Tawi-Tawi — Southern Philippines Patrol Base
sub: Southernmost Philippine province, located near the maritime boundary with Malaysia's Sabah. Philippine Coast Guard and Navy patrol from here into the Sulu Sea. Strategically positioned to monitor Chinese maritime activity in the southern SCS and approach to the Celebes Sea.

label: Naval Base Camilo Osias — New EDCA Site
sub: One of four new EDCA sites announced February 2023 by Secretary Austin and President Marcos. Located in Santa Ana, Cagayan, northern Luzon—less than 400 km from the Bashi Channel and Taiwan. Provides US warship port access, repair facilities, and pre-positioned supplies near Taiwan and Luzon Strait.

label: Lal-Lo Airport — New EDCA Site
sub: New EDCA site in Cagayan, northern Luzon (April 2023). Alternate airfield for US fighter jet refueling and rearming. Strategically positioned to extend the range of US air operations toward Taiwan and the Luzon Strait. Three of the four new EDCA sites are in northern Luzon, facing Taiwan.

label: Camp Melchor Dela Cruz — New EDCA Site
sub: New EDCA site in Gamu, Isabela, northern Luzon (April 2023). HQ of Philippine Army's 5th Infantry Division; hosts a military hospital. Provides US land-based air defense positioning in northern Luzon. US committed to raising EDCA infrastructure investment from $82M to over $100M by end of FY2023.

label: Balabac Island — New EDCA Site
sub: New EDCA site in southernmost Palawan (April 2023). Located 330 km from the center of the Spratly Islands, dominating the Sulu Sea passage. Provides US forces with a southern base flanking the Spratly Islands. Strategically balances the northern Luzon EDCA sites to create multi-directional coverage. UPDATE (Aug 19, 2026): Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim said the Philippines' expanded facilities on Balabac — including a new 3km airstrip and naval infrastructure funded via EDCA — lie roughly 50km (about 20 minutes by vessel) from Malaysia's Banggi Island, Sabah, prompting Malaysia to announce plans to add battalions to Sabah's brigades, stand up a 155mm artillery regiment, install coastal radar, and acquire a Turkish-built Multi-Purpose Command Platform and ANKA reconnaissance drones.

label: Basa Air Base (Cesar Basa AFB)
sub: One of the original five EDCA sites since 2014. Major PAF fighter base 64 km northwest of Manila. 8,000 ft runway. First major EDCA infrastructure project (humanitarian warehouse) activated January 2019. Hosts US pre-positioned equipment and provides rapid response capability for South China Sea contingencies.

label: Antonio Bautista Air Base — Palawan EDCA
sub: One of the original five EDCA sites. Located on Palawan island, directly facing the contested West Philippine Sea. Key air base for Philippine Air Force and US rotational forces monitoring Spratly Islands and EEZ intrusions. Nearest Philippine military airfield to Second Thomas Shoal.

label: Fort Magsaysay — EDCA Ground Training Site
sub: Largest Philippine Army reservation (53,000 ha) in Nueva Ecija, central Luzon. One of the original five EDCA sites. Used for major joint ground force exercises including Balikatan. Hosts HIMARS and Patriot missile system deployments during exercises. US has invested significantly in training ranges here.

label: Andersen Air Force Base — Guam
sub: Major USAF base on Guam; key staging hub for B-1B, B-2, and B-52 bomber rotations covering the Indo-Pacific. Hosts MQ-9 drones and F-22/F-35 fighter detachments. Located ~3,000 km east of the South China Sea; within range of DF-26 'Guam Killer' missile. Continuously upgraded for a potential Taiwan contingency.

label: Naval Base Guam (Apra Harbor)
sub: Only US submarine base west of Hawaii. Hosts Los Angeles-class SSNs and Virginia-class forward-deployed submarines. Key logistics hub for US carrier and surface combatant operations in the western Pacific. Targeted by Chinese DF-26 'Guam Killer' ASBM doctrine. US investing heavily in base hardening and missile defense.

label: Cam Ranh Bay — Vietnam Naval Base
sub: Vietnam's premier deep-water naval facility; finest natural harbor in Southeast Asia. Soviet/Russian naval base 1979–2002. Vietnam People's Navy now operates from here, monitoring South China Sea disputes. US Navy port visits increasingly frequent under US-Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2023). Provides alternative logistics access for Western Pacific operations.

label: Singapore — US Naval Access Hub
sub: Changi Naval Base hosts US Littoral Combat Ships on rotating deployments. Singapore grants the US access under a 2005 Strategic Framework Agreement. Singapore's annual Shangri-La Dialogue is the Indo-Pacific's premier security forum. Singapore navigates carefully between US and China ties, reflecting ASEAN's broader strategic tension.

label: South China Sea — US Carrier Operating Area
sub: Approximate operating area for US carrier strike groups in the South China Sea. Dual-carrier exercises conducted July 2020 (USS Nimitz + USS Ronald Reagan) for first time since 2014. US carriers routinely operate within range of Chinese DF-21D and DF-26 anti-ship ballistic missiles. FONOPs conducted within 12 nm of Chinese-occupied Spratly Islands.

label: Luzon Strait — NMESIS Anti-Ship Deployment
sub: 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment deployed NMESIS truck-mounted Naval Strike Missile launchers to Batanes Islands in the Luzon Strait during Balikatan 2025 (April–May 2025). First overseas deployment outside the US. With ~100 nm range, NMESIS can deny Chinese naval transit through the Luzon Strait between the Pacific and South China Sea.

label: Spratly Islands — Disputed Archipelago
sub: Contested by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, and Brunei. China has the largest military presence through three fully militarized artificial islands. The 2016 PCA ruling found most features generate only a 12 nm territorial sea or no maritime zone at all. Underlain by significant hydrocarbon reserves.

label: Paracel Islands — China-Controlled, Vietnam Claimed
sub: Administered by China since seizing from South Vietnam in January 1974 (Battle of the Paracel Islands; ~75 Vietnamese killed). Vietnam continues to claim as 'Hoang Sa' archipelago. China has militarized the Paracels extensively, with Woody Island hosting a runway, SAMs, fighters, and administrative center for Sansha City.

label: Natuna Islands — Indonesia-China Overlap
sub: Indonesia's northernmost islands, whose EEZ overlaps with China's nine-dash line claim. Indonesia does not consider itself an SCS claimant, but has repeatedly confronted Chinese fishing vessels and CCG ships in Natuna waters (2019, 2020, 2021). Indonesia deployed warships and F-16s after Chinese incursions. Beijing claims 'traditional fishing rights' in Indonesian EEZ.

label: Vanguard Bank — Vietnam EEZ Dispute
sub: Underwater bank within Vietnam's claimed EEZ, near significant gas deposits. China's Haiyang Dizhi 8 survey vessel operated in Vanguard Bank area from July–October 2019, escorted by CCG ships, prompting Vietnamese and Chinese vessel standoffs. US State Department (July 2020) specifically cited Vanguard Bank as an area where China has 'no lawful maritime claim.'

label: James Shoal — China's Southernmost Claim
sub: Submerged bank ~80 km off the coast of Malaysian Sarawak. China claims as its southernmost territorial limit based on the nine-dash line, despite the shoal being permanently underwater (not an island). UNCLOS does not recognize sovereignty over submerged features. China's PLAN has conducted oath-taking ceremonies here. Within Malaysia's EEZ.

label: Luconia Shoals — Malaysia EEZ
sub: Located within Malaysia's EEZ, the Luconia Shoals have been subject to persistent Chinese Coast Guard presence since 2013. Malaysia quietly protests but avoids public confrontation. US (July 2020) specifically cited Luconia Shoals as an area where China has 'no lawful maritime claim.' Home to significant gas reserves exploited by PETRONAS.

label: Brunei EEZ — Chinese Overlap Zone
sub: China's nine-dash line overlaps with Brunei's entire offshore EEZ, encompassing Brunei's productive hydrocarbon fields. Brunei is an ASEAN member and SCS claimant that has avoided direct confrontation with China. US (July 2020) cited Brunei's EEZ as an area where China's nine-dash line claim has no legal basis.

label: Nine-Dash Line — Central Contested Zone
sub: China's claimed boundary encompasses approximately 90% of the South China Sea. The PCA (2016) found it has 'no legal basis' under UNCLOS to the extent it exceeds permitted entitlements. The US formally rejected the claim July 13, 2020. The nine-dash line overlaps with the EEZs of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, and Indonesia.

label: Lombok Strait — AUKUS Submarine Transit
sub: Strategic deep-water strait between Bali and Lombok, Indonesia. Primary transit route for nuclear-powered submarines avoiding the shallow Malacca Strait. AUKUS submarines from HMAS Stirling (Western Australia) would transit through Lombok Strait to reach the South China Sea. Indonesia does not permit foreign nuclear-powered submarines in its territorial waters, requiring deep-water transits.

label: Strait of Malacca — Strategic Chokepoint
sub: World's most strategically important shipping lane: 85,000+ transits per year, 30%+ of global trade. One-third of world's oil supply transits through here. A major conflict in the South China Sea could disrupt Malacca Strait traffic, triggering global economic crisis. China's 'Malacca Dilemma': dependence on this US Navy-secured strait makes it a strategic vulnerability.

label: Singapore — AUKUS Diplomatic & Logistics Hub
sub: Host of annual Shangri-La Dialogue (IISS Asia Security Summit). US has rotating Littoral Combat Ships at Changi Naval Base. Key neutral diplomatic space for US-China and AUKUS engagement. Singapore has expressed concern about being 'forced to choose' between US and China while maintaining military cooperation with both.

label: Luzon Strait — First Island Chain Chokepoint
sub: ~250 km wide between Luzon (Philippines) and Taiwan. Critical chokepoint for PLAN surface and submarine transit between the South China Sea and Pacific Ocean. 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment with NMESIS deployed here during Balikatan 2025 to demonstrate US ability to deny PLAN freedom of movement. Key battleground in any Taiwan contingency.

label: Balikatan 2024 Exercise Zone — Outside Territorial Waters
sub: Balikatan 2024 (April–May 2024) marked the first time exercises were held outside the Philippines' 12 nm territorial waters, directly challenging Chinese EEZ claims. France participated as full partner for the first time. 16,000 troops from US, Philippines, Australia, France. A live-fire missile test struck a target vessel. China protested the exercises.

label: Taiwan Strait — China's Declared 'Internal Waters'
sub: China claims the Taiwan Strait as 'internal waters,' rejecting the traditional median line concept. PLA conducted record incursions across the median line: 23 total crossings before Pelosi visit (Aug 2022), then 563 in 2022 alone. Multiple PLA exercise encirclements (2022, 2023, 2024) simulated Taiwan blockade scenarios. US maintains freedom of navigation transits through the strait.

label: Lumbia Air Base — Mindanao EDCA Site
sub: One of the original five EDCA sites since 2014, located in Cagayan de Oro, Mindanao. Provides US forces with access to the southern Philippines, relevant for operations in the Sulu Sea and toward the southern Spratly Islands. Philippine Air Force and US rotational forces use the base for exercises and contingency pre-positioning.

label: Tree Island (Ile des Arbres) — China Paracel Outpost
sub: Small island in the Paracel Islands controlled by China since 1974. Part of the Crescent Group of the Paracels; hosts a Chinese military garrison and monitoring equipment. Previously occupied by South Vietnam; China seized all Paracel Islands in the Battle of the Paracel Islands, January 19, 1974.

label: Phu Lam (Yongxing) — Vietnam's Claimed 'Hoang Sa'
sub: Woody Island is the administrative center of China's Sansha City but is also claimed by Vietnam as part of 'Hoang Sa' (Paracel Islands). Vietnam's official position is that China's 1974 seizure was an illegal act of aggression, and Vietnam has never relinquished its claim. Vietnam periodically protests Chinese administrative actions on this island.

label: Recto Bank — 2019 FB Gem-Ver Sinking
sub: Chinese fishing vessel F/V Yuemaobinyu 42212 struck and sank Philippine fishing boat FB Gem-Ver at Reed Bank (Recto Bank) on June 9, 2019, abandoning 22 Filipino fishermen. Vietnamese fishermen rescued the crew. The incident triggered massive political backlash against Duterte's pro-China stance and remains a flashpoint for Philippine public opinion on the South China Sea.

label: Balikatan 2026 — Exercise Zone (Apr 20–May 8, 2026)
sub: Main exercise area for Balikatan 2026, the largest-ever iteration with 17,000+ troops from 7 nations (Philippines, US, Japan, Australia, Canada, France, New Zealand) and 17 observer nations. Japan deploys Type 88 anti-ship missiles — first combat-capable Japanese overseas exercise deployment since WWII. Training areas reach within 120 nm of Scarborough Shoal. Exercise runs April 20–May 8, 2026.

label: Coast Guard District Kalayaan Island Group — Activated Apr 9, 2026
sub: Philippines activated the Coast Guard District Kalayaan Island Group at Pag-asa Island on April 9, 2026 — the first dedicated PCG district-level command in the Spratly Islands. The facility is designed to improve response times to CCG and maritime militia incursions in the Kalayaan Island Group. Chinese coast guard vessels issued radio warnings to Philippine aircraft and fired flares at patrol aircraft near Subi Reef and Mischief Reef on the same day as the activation ceremony.

label: China Fires Flares at Philippine Aircraft — Mischief Reef Area, Apr 9, 2026
sub: Chinese coast guard forces fired warning flares at Philippine patrol aircraft near Subi Reef and Mischief Reef on April 9, 2026, coinciding with the Philippines' activation of its new Coast Guard District Kalayaan Island Group at Pagasa Island. The Philippines called the incident a 'clear and deliberate act of bullying.' Use of aerial flares against government aircraft is escalatory beyond water cannons and represents the second flare incident in the Spratlys in under three weeks (after March 20 at Mischief Reef).

label: Quanzhou — 11th BCM / 24th FMC Talks
sub: Site of the 11th Philippines-China Bilateral Consultation Mechanism (BCM) and 24th Foreign Ministry Consultations (FMC) on the South China Sea, held March 27–28, 2026. Led by Philippine DFA Undersecretary Leo Herrera-Lim and Chinese Vice FM Sun Weidong. Talks covered SCS maritime tensions, oil and gas cooperation dialogue, coast guard communication, and planning for a foreign ministers' meeting 'within the year.' First BCM since January 2025; first FMC since March 2023.

label: Camp Aguinaldo — Balikatan 2026 Opening Ceremony (Apr 20)
sub: Site of the official opening ceremony for Exercise Balikatan 41-2026 on April 20, 2026. AFP Chief General Romeo Brawner Jr. declared the exercise officially open. Attended by senior commanders from all 7 participating nations (PH, US, Japan, Australia, Canada, France, NZ) and representatives of 18 observer nations. Japan's Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi attended. China's FM condemned the exercise as 'playing with fire' on opening day.

label: BrahMos Regiment — Northern Luzon (Balikatan 2026 Strike Drill)
sub: Philippine Marines' BrahMos supersonic cruise missile regiment position in northern Luzon for Balikatan 2026. On April 21 (Day 2), the regiment conducted simulated firing in a trilateral maritime strike drill with US and Japanese forces, targeting decommissioned vessels — the first multilateral BrahMos exercise in the Philippines. Range: 290 km at Mach 2.8; covers South China Sea approaches and Luzon Strait corridor.

label: Type 076 'Drone Carrier' Sichuan — SCS Sea Trials (Apr 22, 2026)
sub: China's first Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan commenced South China Sea sea trials on April 22, 2026 — its first-ever SCS deployment. Announced by PLA Navy as 'scientific research trials and training missions.' The Sichuan features CATOBAR electromagnetic catapults for launching UCAVs (GJ-21 stealth attack drone), a stern well dock for landing craft, and twin-island superstructure. ~45,000 tons. Deployment coincides with Balikatan 2026 and Liaoning carrier group operations in the same waters. Commissioning expected late 2026 – early 2027.

label: Naval Station Leovigildo Gantioqui (NSLG) — Balikatan 2026 IAMD Phase
sub: Naval Station Leovigildo Gantioqui (NSLG) in San Antonio, Zambales hosted the Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD) phase of Balikatan 2026 starting April 26, 2026. Four-day drills (April 26–29) linked radar systems, command centers, and missile defense batteries (US Patriot PAC-3, MADIS, Philippine Air Force networks) to detect and neutralize simulated aerial and ballistic missile threats. Location on the Luzon western seaboard provides direct coverage of South China Sea approaches. US contributors: ~1,300 Marines and sailors from 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment (Kaneohe Bay) and 25th Infantry Division (Schofield Barracks).

label: Long Point Beach, Palawan — Balikatan 2026 Day 8 Counter-Landing Live Fire
sub: Site of Balikatan 2026 Day 8 counter-landing live-fire exercise (April 27, 2026) at Barangay Aporawan, Aborlan, Palawan — facing the South China Sea. US, Philippine, New Zealand, and Australian service members executed amphibious denial drills featuring HIMARS rocket systems and unmanned systems/drone integration, marking the most technologically advanced combined amphibious exercise in Philippine territory. The western Palawan location directly faces the West Philippine Sea and South China Sea approach from the Spratly Islands.

label: PLA Zunyi Type 055 — YJ-20 Hypersonic Exercise East of Luzon, Apr 27, 2026
sub: Position of Chinese Type 055 destroyer Zunyi during PLA exercises east of Luzon on April 27, 2026. PLA released footage of the Zunyi firing a YJ-20 hypersonic anti-ship cruise missile — range 1,000–1,500 km, Mach 6+ cruise, Mach 10 terminal — as a direct counter-signal during Balikatan 2026's second week. From this position, the YJ-20 can engage targets throughout the South China Sea, Philippine Sea, and Luzon Strait corridor. South China Morning Post reported the footage was intended to demonstrate counter-force capability against allied naval formations. Timed to coincide with Balikatan 2026 Day 8 counter-landing drills in Palawan.

label: Itu Aba (Taiping Island) — Taiwan-Administered, Spratly Islands
sub: Largest naturally occurring island in the Spratly Islands (~0.46 sq km); administered by Taiwan (Republic of China) since 1956. Hosts ~200 Coast Guard and military personnel, an airstrip, desalination plant, and medical facility. Taiwan's Ocean Affairs Council Minister Kuan Bi-ling visited Itu Aba and nearby Zhongzhou Reef on April 28, 2026 amid Balikatan 2026 tensions, asserting Taiwan's SCS claims. Claimed by Taiwan, China, Philippines, and Vietnam. Under Taiwan's Nansha Islands administrative designation, concurrent with PRC's nine-dash line.

label: Cebu — 48th ASEAN Summit (May 7-8, 2026)
sub: Host city for the 48th ASEAN Leaders Summit (May 7-8, 2026), the ASEAN-EU Sustainability Summit (May 7), and associated ministerial meetings. As of April 29, 2026, Philippine authorities reported 80% readiness with 10,000 police deploying for security. Key agenda: South China Sea Code of Conduct negotiations, Myanmar reintegration, ASEAN-EU relations. Malaysia PM Anwar Ibrahim (2026 ASEAN Chair) has pledged to fast-track a binding COC. Philippines DFA Secretary Lazaro has called the COC 'something we owe the world.'

label: PLA Naval Action Group — Luzon Strait Vicinity, Apr 28, 2026
sub: A Chinese naval action group operated in proximity to US missile deployments near the Taiwan approach / Luzon Strait area on April 28, 2026, as reported by USNI News. This is assessed as distinct from PLA Task Group 107 (which drilled east of Luzon on April 24-25). The simultaneous presence of US missiles near the Taiwan approach and this PLA action group in the Luzon Strait creates an active bilateral deterrence dynamic at the northern chokepoint of the Philippine archipelago — the most sensitive single waterway for any Taiwan contingency.

label: DESRON-7/Task Force Ashland MME — NOLCOM Area, Apr 28-29, 2026
sub: DESRON-7 and Task Force Ashland commenced Multinational Maritime Events (MME) with Philippine Navy, HMCS Charlottetown (Canada), and JMSDF ships in the Northern Luzon Command (NOLCOM) area on April 28-29, 2026 (Balikatan 2026 Days 9-10). Luzon Strait corridor exercises directly border the Bashi Channel between northern Luzon and Taiwan. Combined US-Philippine-Canadian-Japanese naval maneuvering and sea control drills at a chokepoint where a Chinese naval action group was simultaneously operating, per USNI News (April 28).

label: PLA STC Combat Readiness Patrols — Scarborough Shoal, Apr 30, 2026
sub: On April 30, 2026 (Balikatan 2026 Day 11), the PLA Southern Theater Command announced naval and air force 'combat readiness patrols' at Huangyan Dao (Scarborough Shoal). Framed as 'effective countermeasures' to Balikatan 2026. China Coast Guard conducted simultaneous law-enforcement patrols. AFP called it 'information operations designed to project a false sense of control.' Combined with Task Group 107 (east Luzon, Apr 24-25) and the Luzon Strait action group (Apr 28), China is now conducting simultaneous counter-posturing at three axes around the Philippine archipelago. Source: Xinhua (April 30, 2026).

label: Balikatan 2026 Day 11: 11-Ship MME — West Philippine Sea, Apr 30, 2026
sub: On April 30, 2026 (Day 11), AFP and 4 allied navies deployed 11 warships in the West Philippine Sea: BRP Miguel Malvar, BRP Antonio Luna (Philippines); USS Ashland (US); JS Ikazuchi, JS Shimokita (Japan); HMAS Toowoomba (Australia). Exercises: COMCHECK, PHOTOEX, CASEX (anti-submarine), GUNNEX. Chinese vessels shadowed from a distance without dangerous maneuvers. Largest allied naval grouping ever exercised in the West Philippine Sea under Balikatan. Source: Manila Bulletin (April 30, 2026).

label: Sandy Cay 1 — Atin Ito Flag Planting / China 'Illegal Research' Confrontation (May 3, 2026)
sub: On May 3, 2026, Filipino civilian coalition Atin Ito sailed overnight and planted the Philippine flag on Sandy Cay 1 in the Spratly Islands. China's Coast Guard accused five Philippine nationals of 'illegal landing.' Philippines identified four Chinese vessels conducting what it termed 'illegal research' at the feature and threatened to deploy aircraft and ships to expel them. Sandy Cay 1 is a low-lying sandbar near Philippines-administered Thitu Island (Pag-asa) in the Kalayaan Island Group, approximately 160 nm from Palawan — well within the Philippines' EEZ. The confrontation opened a new front in the civilian-led sovereignty assertion campaign alongside the BRP Sierra Madre garrison at Second Thomas Shoal. Source: Malay Mail, Free Malaysia Today, OneNews.PH (May 3, 2026).

label: La Paz Sand Dunes, Laoag — CLLFX-N, Balikatan 2026 Day 15 (May 4, 2026)
sub: Site of the Counter-Landing Live Fire Exercise North (CLLFX-N) during Balikatan 2026 on May 4, 2026. Philippine, US, and Japanese forces executed high-intensity combined-arms drills featuring HIMARS rocket systems, Apache Longbow attack helicopters, and 105mm howitzers at La Paz Sand Dunes in Laoag, Ilocos Norte. The exercise simulated defense of Northern Luzon's coastline against a mock amphibious invasion, testing allied forces' ability to detect, intercept, and repel hostile landing operations. Located in the northwestern tip of Luzon directly facing the Luzon Strait — the critical chokepoint between Luzon and Taiwan. Sources: PNA, Manila Bulletin, Manila Times (May 4, 2026).

label: Balikatan 2026 SINKEX — Target Vessel Zone Off Ilocos Norte (May 6, 2026)
sub: Location where Japan, US, Australia, and Philippine forces conducted a Ship Sinking Exercise (SINKEX) on May 6, 2026 (Balikatan Day 17), firing anti-ship missiles to sink a decommissioned vessel off Ilocos Norte. Japan's participation marks the first combat troop deployment by Japan to the Philippines since WWII — a landmark post-war pivot in Japan's overseas defense engagement (Bloomberg, May 6, 2026). Located in the South China Sea off Ilocos Norte, the northernmost province of Luzon, directly facing the Luzon Strait approach between Luzon and Taiwan. Complements CLLFX-N at same location May 4.

label: 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit — Mactan Expo, Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu (May 8, 2026)
sub: Venue for the 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit on May 8, 2026, chaired by President Marcos as 2026 ASEAN Host. Theme: 'Navigating Our Future, Together.' Preceded by Senior Officials' meetings (May 6) and Foreign Ministers' meeting (May 7) at Shangri-La Mactan. Over 20,000 delegates from all 10 ASEAN member states plus EU and 20+ dialogue partners. South China Sea Code of Conduct tops the agenda. Schedule compressed from 5 to 3 days (May 6-8) by presidential directive. Marcos declared local holidays in Lapu-Lapu City and Cordova. Security: 10,000+ police, 1,000+ AFP, PSC.

label: Scarborough Shoal — China 'Marine Nature Reserve' Claim (May 2026)
sub: China declared a 'marine nature reserve' at Scarborough Shoal (Huangyan Dao) in May 2026, triggering a Philippine DFA diplomatic protest (May 11). Former SC Justice Antonio Carpio warned (May 10) this mirrors China's civilian-to-military conversion playbook at Fiery Cross and Subi Reefs — where 'environmental' installations later became missile battery sites. Combined with the April 2026 floating barrier and CCG Chuanshan training (May 9), the marine nature reserve represents a new institutional pressure vector at the disputed feature. Under UNCLOS and the 2016 PCA ruling, no state may establish a nature reserve in contested waters excluding another state's nationals from traditional fishing grounds without consent.

label: Vietnam Spratly Outpost Expansion — 2025–2026
sub: Bloomberg (May 9, 2026) and SCMP confirmed Vietnam added approximately 534 acres of reclaimed land in the Spratly Islands over the past year, bringing its total to ~2,771 acres — second-largest in the archipelago after China's ~5,460 acres. Vietnam now has 15 harbors in the Spratlys, with 11 created since 2021; three new harbors under construction at Grierson Reef, Petley Reef, and South Reef. Vietnam administers 21+ Spratly features including Spratly Island (Truong Sa Lon), Southwest Cay, Sin Cowe Island, East Reef, and Union Banks features. Unlike China's 2013–2016 mass reclamation, Vietnam's expansion is gradual, harbor-focused, and concentrated around features it has administered since the 1970s. No military confrontation associated with Vietnam's construction. Simultaneous with China's Antelope Reef expansion in the Paracels (~1,490 acres by April 2026). Sources: Bloomberg, SCMP, The Star Malaysia (May 9, 2026).

label: Scarborough Shoal — 8 PLAN Warships + 9 CCG Post-Balikatan (May 2026)
sub: AFP WPS monitoring report (May 13, 2026) documents 8 PLA Navy warships and 9 China Coast Guard cutters concentrated at Scarborough Shoal during the May 4-11 monitoring window — the largest combined China military presence at Scarborough officially recorded in AFP public reporting. This deployment coincides with China's ongoing 'marine nature reserve' institutional claim (DFA protest May 11, no Chinese response), the April 10-11 floating barrier, and the CCG Chuanshan rights-safeguarding training (May 9). Total WPS footprint: 35 Chinese vessels at 4 locations. The PLAN warship concentration at Scarborough—post-Balikatan 2026—is assessed as China signaling deterrence consolidation at its most institutionally sensitive disputed feature. Source: Philstar / AFP, May 13, 2026.

label: Sandy Cay 2/3 — Chinese Personnel Landing (Pag-asa Territorial Sea), May 18, 2026
sub: On May 16-17 (reported May 18, 2026), Chinese personnel from research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 were ferried via RHIBs and rubber boats onto Sandy Cay 2 (Cay-2) and Sandy Cay 3 (Cay-3) — both within the 12-nautical-mile territorial sea of Pag-asa (Thitu) Island. CCG vessels 5101 and 5309 escorted the research vessel. PCG Islander aircraft 4177 flew repeated challenges. PCG launched a formal investigation and dismissed China's 'stunt' characterization. First documented Chinese personnel landing on Philippine-claimed Spratly sandbars since modern Philippine monitoring began — qualitative escalation from EEZ violation (Reed Bank phase) to territorial sea incursion. China's Global Times framed the incident as PCG 'harassment' at 'Houteng Jiao.' Sources: Philippine Star, PNA, SunStar, PTV News (May 18, 2026).

label: CCG Vessel 4305 — Unauthorized Patrol 48nm Off Zambales, May 19, 2026
sub: China Coast Guard vessel CCG 4305 was detected approximately 48–50.1 nautical miles west of Pandaquit, Zambales on May 19, 2026 — within the Philippine EEZ off Luzon's western coast. Flagged by Canada's Dark Vessel Detection (DVS) Program. PCG Piper Navajo aircraft 302 confirmed visually at 8:40 a.m. BRP Cape San Agustin dispatched to challenge. Chinese vessel ignored all radio challenges. PCG Commandant Admiral Gavan pledged to 'never allow normalization of illegal patrols' off Zambales. Second simultaneous EEZ intrusion on May 19 alongside Xiang Yang Hong 33 operations near Pag-asa Island — a multi-vector Chinese maritime pressure campaign extending to the Luzon western coast. Sources: Philippine Star, Manila Bulletin, GMA News, Newsweek, PNA (May 19, 2026).

label: Shangri-La Dialogue 2026 — AUKUS Defence Ministerial (May 30, 2026)
sub: The 21st IISS Shangri-La Dialogue (May 30 – June 1, 2026) at the Shangri-La Hotel, Singapore, hosted the AUKUS Defence Ministerial on May 30 — US SecDef Hegseth, UK DefSec Healey, and Australian DefMin Marles announced the first AUKUS Pillar II signature project: joint development of UUV payloads, delivery beginning 2027. Australia confirmed to receive secondhand Virginia-class submarines. All three partners reaffirmed AUKUS commitment to the submarine pathway and Indo-Pacific deterrence against the backdrop of ongoing South China Sea tensions.

label: Scarborough Shoal Floating Platform — Confirmed Removed, June 17, 2026
sub: The 6-by-6-meter floating research platform China installed inside Bajo de Masinloc's (Scarborough Shoal) lagoon — first discovered by Philippine authorities on May 25, 2026 and the subject of a formal Philippine protest and probe — was confirmed removed during final-day surveillance of the 4th PH-US Bilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity on June 17, 2026. China had claimed the structure was a 'temporary scientific research facility' studying coral reefs; Manila rejected that characterization. Two earlier floating buoys China installed in October 2025 remained in place. Sources: CSIS Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative, Manila Bulletin (June 20, 2026).

label: Exercise Salaknib 2026 — Luzon-wide Operational Maneuver Drills, June 1-16, 2026
sub: The Philippine Army and US Army (25th Infantry Division) conducted the Operational Maneuver (OPMAN) phase of Exercise Salaknib 2026 across multiple Luzon training sites (June 1-16), for the first time incorporating Japan Ground Self-Defense Force troops alongside Australian and New Zealand elements as part of a ~7,000-troop multinational program. Training spanned maritime security, ground maneuver, strategic airlift, precision fires, and air-assault operations. Sources: Tribune Philippines, US Army (June 18, 2026).

label: 10th Anniversary of SCS Arbitral Award — National Peace Walk, Manila, July 12, 2026
sub: On the 10th anniversary of the July 12, 2016 Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling rejecting China's 'nine-dash line' claims, the Philippines and 13 other countries (US, Australia, Canada, Estonia, Germany, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Lithuania, New Zealand, Romania, Slovenia, UK) plus the EU issued a joint statement reaffirming the award as 'final, legally binding, and definitive.' Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and AFP Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr. joined thousands of Filipinos in a National Peace Walk to the Quirino Grandstand. China's Foreign Ministry rejected the ruling as 'null and void.' ASEAN as a bloc declined to join the joint statement. Sources: US State Department, Manila Times, Irish Times (July 12-13, 2026).

label: PH Sailor Struck With Baton
sub: CCG personnel struck a Philippine Navy sailor's head with a wooden baton near BRP Sierra Madre, Jul 20, 2026

label: Scarborough Water-Cannon Clashes
sub: China Coast Guard fired water cannons at Philippine vessels twice (Jul 23, Jul 24), the 2nd and 3rd clashes of a three-clash week

label: 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting
sub: Manila hosts AMM Jul 18-24; ministers pledge to finalize SCS Code of Conduct by end-2026

label: USS George Washington CSG Patrol
sub: US carrier strike group patrols the South China Sea amid Philippines-China tensions, reported Jul 27, 2026

label: Scarborough 'Nature Reserve' Fishing Ban Rules
sub: China releases rules banning unauthorized fishing, mining and coral harvesting at its Scarborough Shoal nature reserve, Aug 1, 2026

label: China Warship + Bomber Surge
sub: Type 052D DDG, Type 071 LPD, Type 054A FFG, Type 056A corvette + H-6K bombers surge to Scarborough Shoal, Aug 1-3, 2026

label: Sandy Cay (Tiexian Jiao) — China Ecological Report
sub: China's Ministry of Natural Resources says live coral coverage at Sandy Cay has fallen ~70% since 2016, blaming Philippine construction/fishing at nearby Thitu Island; report released amid US-China dispute over Scarborough Shoal 'nature reserve,' Aug 14, 2026

label: RORE Mission to BRP Sierra Madre
sub: BRP Malabrigo and BRP Teresa Magbanua ran a resupply mission to Ayungin Shoal, shadowed by CCG and militia vessels, Aug 22, 2026

label: 19th MMCA — Sabina Shoal Radio Challenge
sub: Chinese warship 536 radioed BRP Diego Silang near Sabina Shoal during the PH-US-Australia 19th MMCA, asserting sovereignty and ordering it to leave; Manila rejected the claim citing UNCLOS, Aug 21-25, 2026
